answer:
Their roles in the nighttime escapes are completely reversed. In Chapter 11, before the closed door, Udayaditya draws his sword and orders Sitaram, “Defend yourself; come at me.” Sitaram does not resist: he offers up his own weapon and begs to be bound from head to toe, then presses his forehead to the dust at the Crown Prince’s feet. In other words, the Crown Prince is the one who decides whether to restrain or release the concubine’s attendant, while Sitaram offers his life—his life before the Maharaja the next day—and sides with the palace’s order.

In Chapter 29, that reversal takes place. Now a prisoner, Udayaditya is the one who asks “Why?” when Sitaram opens the door and comes in. When Sitaram says, “Please go outside,” Udayaditya does as he is told, is seized, and is led out of the prison, almost as if he were being carried. Once they reach the open fields, the Crown Prince repeatedly asks, at a loss, “What should I do? Where should I go?” and finally entrusts Sitaram with leading him, saying, “Come, please come with me.”

Thus, the one who gave orders and bound the other has become the one who gives directions, while the other is led at his command. Moreover, the man who in Chapter 11 said, “I cannot defy you,” and allowed himself to be bound now openly defies the palace’s order—the Crown Prince’s imprisonment—and takes him out. The man who in Chapter 11 worried about his own safety, asking, “What shall I say to the Maharaja tomorrow?” now risks himself to free the Crown Prince. Even the direction of the debt between them—the one whose life was saved and who submitted to being bound, and the one whose life was saved and who follows instructions—has turned back on itself between the two, not merely their relative positions.
answer_ja:
夜の脱出をめぐる二人の位置関係は完全に上下を入れ替えている。第11章では、閉ざされた扉の前でウダヤディティヤが剣を抜いてシタラムに「刃向かえ、かかってこい」と命令し、シタラムは逆らわず自らの武器を差し出して頭のてっぺんから足の先まで縛るよう懇願し、王太子の足元の塵を額にいただく。つまり、王太子が決裁者として仕妾の身柄を拘束・解除し、シタラムは己の命（明日マハラジャの前での命）を差し出して宮殿の秩序に従った側に回る。

第29章ではその逆転が起きる。囚われの身となったウダヤディティヤは、扉を開けて中へ入ってくるシタラムに「なぜだ？」と質問する側にまわる。シタラムが「外へ出てください」と言うと、彼は言われるがまま掴まれ、ほとんど抱えられるようにして牢獄の外へ連れ出される。野原に出た王太子は「どうすればいい？どこへ行けばいい？」と途方に暮れて繰り返し尋ね、最後は「さあ、私と一緒に来てください」とシタラムに案内を委ねる。

すなわち、命令して縛った者／縛られた者が、指示する者／指示されて導かれる者に反転した。しかも第11章で「刃向かうことはできない」と言いながら自ら拘束された側が、今度は宮殿の秩序（王太子の幽閉）に公然と刃向かって人を運び出し、第11章では「明日マハラジャにどう申し上げるか」と自らの身の安全を気にしていた男が、今回は王太子の解放に自らの身を危険にさらす側へ回っている。命を救われて従順に拘束された者と、命を救われて指示を受ける者という借りと返しの向きも、単なる上下ではなく二人の間に逆流している。

answer:
The initial plan was to have two Pathans (Pashtuns) assassinate Basanta Ray when he stopped at an inn in Simultali on his way to Jessore. But the elder of the two Pathans led the attendants away with a rumor about bandits in the village, leaving the plotters behind, so the plan failed. The remaining Pathan was also found out by the crown prince Udayaditya and confessed to the plot; in the end, he even sought Basanta Ray’s protection.

Ultimately, after capturing Udayaditya in the fields, Pratapaditya sent Mukhtiyar Khan with a signed death warrant and had him carry out the execution of the king of Raigarh (Basanta Ray). The warrant was delivered to Basanta Ray as he was saying his evening prayers. When he gave up and evasively said, “Do your duty,” Abdul, acting on Mukhtiyar’s orders, drew his sword and struck him down. The old king was killed inside the palace.
answer_ja:
最初の計画は、バサンタ・ライがジョソールへ向かう道中、シムルタリの宿に立ち寄った際に、二人のパターン人（パシュトゥーン人）に暗殺を命じたものだった。しかし、そのパターン人の兄が従者たちを村の盗賊の噂で引き連れ、仕掛け人を残して追い払ったため失敗に終わり、残されたパターン人本人も王太子ウダヤディティヤに看破されて計画を自白し、かえってバサンタ・ライの保護を求める有様だった。

最終的には、ウダヤディティヤを野原で捕らえた後、ムクティヤール・カーンに署名入りの死刑命令書を携えさせ、ライガルの王（バサンタ・ライ）の処刑を遂行させた。夕べの祈りを捧げていたバサンタ・ライに命令書が渡され、彼が諦めて「そなたの命令を果たすがよい」と言葉を濁すと、ムクティヤールの命を受けたアブドゥルが抜き身の剣をもってこれを斬り、老王は室内で殺害された。

answer: The first was when, disguised as a woman and pretending to be an old woman, he was grabbed by the neck in the queen’s chambers (among the women of the inner palace), tied up with a shawl, and carried out. The second was when, in his usual guise as the jester Ramai Bhand, he was in the king’s chamber (the audience room) and was seized by the scruff of the neck and thrown outside.
answer_ja: 1つ目は、女装して老婆のふりをし、王妃の部屋（奥御殿の女官たちのもと）で首に締め上げられ、ショールで縛られて担ぎ出されたこと。2つ目は、道化（ラマイ・バンド）の本来の姿で王の間（謁見の部屋）に居たところ、首根っこを掴んで部屋の外へ放り出されたこと。

answer: The fact that she had been secretly sending him money reached the king’s ears and was used as a pretext for her exile. But what actually caused Surma to leave was the queen’s secret threat, delivered in private: “If you still refuse to return, I will put Udayaditya in chains and imprison him.” To protect the one she loved, Surma decided to leave of her own accord.
answer_ja: 密かに給金を送っていたことが王の耳に入ったのが追放の口実とされたが、実際にスルマを去らせたのは、王妃が内々に浴びせかけた「それでも帰らねばウダヤディティヤを枷にかけ投獄する」という密かな脅しで、彼女は愛する者の身を守るために自ら出発を決意した。

answer: Because Vibha refused Rammohan’s first escort, saying, “I cannot leave my brother alone,” King Ramchandra Rai of Chandradwip flew into a rage at the insult and, unable either to bring her back or take revenge, grew increasingly frustrated and vengeful. The people, too, became clamorous for revenge, and talk of remarriage arose at court, where the wedding preparations were set in motion. As a result, when Vibha finally arrived later, having gone to Rammohan herself, the Maharaja had already married another woman. Her hope of returning to her husband’s home and regaining happiness as queen vanished like a mirage; she had no place or home left in his kingdom, and with a single blow, her entire world was shattered. Moreover, Rammohan could not face the king, saying, “Your Ladyship did not come,” and Vibha had not only been unable to leave her brother behind, but even Rammohan, whom she dearly loved, left in anger. With no one able to understand her pain, all that remained was isolation and despair.
answer_ja: ビバがラムモハンの最初の迎えを「兄を一人にしては行けない」と拒んだことで、チャンドラドウィープ王ラーマチャンドラ・ライは侮辱に激怒し、迎えも仕返しもできないまま焦燥と復讐心を募らせていった。民衆までもが復讐を求める騒ぎとなり、宮廷では再婚の話が持ち上がって婚礼の支度が決められてしまう。その結果、後日ようやくビバが自らラムモハンを頼って到着したとき、マハラジャはすでに別の女性と結婚した後だった。ビバの夫の家へ帰り、王妃として幸福を取り戻そうとする望みは蜃気楼のように消え失せ、彼女の王国には居場所も家もなくなり、たった一撃で世界のすべてを打ち砕かれることになる。加えて、ラムモハンは「奥方様が来なかった」と王の前で顔を向けられず、ビバも兄を置いて行けなかったばかりか、心から慕うラムモハンまでもが怒って去るという形で、誰一人彼女の痛みを理解してあげられないまま、孤立と絶望だけが残る。

answer: The ring Rukmini received from Udayaditya bore the seal with the crown prince’s name. Bhagavata and Sitaram forged a petition bearing that seal, making it appear that Pratapaditya was being accused of treason against the emperor and was trying to seize the kingdom for himself. Instead of sending the petition to Delhi, Bhagavata handed it to Pratapaditya himself and informed on Udayaditya, saying, “Udayaditya’s retainer was trying to take this to Delhi.” The petition bearing the crown prince’s seal was itself taken as proof that it was in Udayaditya’s own hand, and on that basis he was imprisoned (though the authenticity of the evidence was questioned, the king ordered his imprisonment, saying, “There is no harm in keeping him in prison.”)
answer_ja: ルクミニーがウダヤディティヤから受け取った指輪には、王太子の名の印章が刻まれていた。バーガヴァタとシタラムは、皇帝への反逆罪でプラタパディティヤを告発し、自ら王国を得ようとしているかのように見せる偽の嘆願書を作成し、その印章を押した。バーガヴァタは嘆願書をデリーへ向かうのではなくプラタパディティヤ本人に渡し、「ウダヤディティヤの家来がこれをデリーへ持って行こうとしていた」と告げ口した。王太子の印章が押された嘆願書そのものが王太子の自筆の証拠とみなされ、その根拠としてウダヤディティヤは投獄されることになった（証拠の真偽に疑問は呈されたが、王は「牢に入れておくことに差し支えはない」として投獄を命じた）。

answer: When Ramchandra Ray escaped to a boat at midnight by climbing down Ram Mohan’s rope, the guards who were watching the doors of the inner palace, including Sitaram, could not defy the Crown Prince. They allowed him to escape, either by letting themselves be tied up or by turning a blind eye. Udayaditya learned that those held responsible—Sitaram and the guards who had been dismissed—were in dire straits, and began giving them monthly stipends on his own initiative. When Pratapaditya heard of this, he issued a stern order: “They must not be given stipends.” But it was later discovered that Surma had continued secretly sending the stipends through a trusted maid. Enraged by this, the king ordered Surma to return to her parental home. In short, the treatment of the guards involved in the escape and Udayaditya’s aid to them led to the stipend issue, and the exile order followed when Surma’s secret act of kindness came to light.
answer_ja: ラーマチャンドラ・ライが深夜、ラムモハンの綱を伝って舟へ脱出する際、奥御殿の扉を守っていた衛兵やシタラムらは王太子に刃向かえず、縛られる・見逃す形で脱出を許してしまった。その責任を問われた者たち（シタラムら解雇された衛兵）が困窮したと知ったウダヤディティヤが、自分の判断で月々の俸給を与え始める。これがプラタパディティヤの耳に入り、「俸給を付けてはならぬ」と厳命される。しかしその後もスルマが信頼する侍女を通して密かに俸給を送り続けたことが発覚し、そのことで激怒した王が、スルマを実家へ帰すよう命じる。つまり、脱出劇に絡む卫兵たちの処遇とウダヤディティヤの救済が俸給問題を生み、スルマの内密の善行が露見したことで追放命令につながった。

answer:
The song “I Alone Am Left Behind” expresses the loneliness and pain of loss after losing loved ones—the people with whom one wanted to rejoice and share an embrace. The song rises up naturally, but there is no one left to hear it; whenever joy arose, there was no one anywhere with whom to share it. The loss of singing and the loss of joy overlap, filling the song with the emptiness of the one left alive: a sentiment in which even the memory of joy has faded, leaving “nothing but emptiness for the one left behind.”

Basanta Ray sings this song in two contrasting situations:

1. **A quiet, solitary evening** (on the balcony of the Raigarh palace): Watching the setting sun, he sings as if the song were spilling out of him of its own accord, unnoticed and alone, an old man who has laid aside his sitar. He sings in mute loneliness and remembrance, with no one there to listen.

2. **When someone is by his side** (in front of the dark, empty room in Jassore): After being shown the emptiness of Surma’s room, he takes Biba’s hand and begins to sing quietly and deliberately. He sings alongside Biba, who is like the remnant of a person, sharing her sorrow with her.

In other words, the first is a lonely way of singing, “as if talking to oneself when there is no one to listen,” while the second is an empathetic way of singing, “in connection with someone by one’s side.” The same song thus takes two contrasting forms: isolation and shared grief.
answer_ja:
「私だけが、ただ一人残された」の歌は、愛する者たち――共に喜び、抱きしめたかった者たち――を失った孤独と喪失の痛みを歌うものである。歌は自然に湧き上がるが、それを聴いてくれる相手はもうおらず、喜びが生まれるたびに分かち合いたかった者がどこにもいない。歌うことと喜びの喪失が重なり、生きて残された者の空虚さ、すなわち「残された者はただ虚しいだけ」という、喜びの記憶そのものまでもが絶えてしまった感傷を湛えている。

バサンタ・ライは、次の2つの対照的な状況でこの歌を口ずさむ。

1. **独りぼっちの静かな夕暮れ**（ライガルの宮殿のベランダ）：沈む太陽を見つめながら、シタールを手放した老いた自分が誰にも知られず、ひとりでにこぼれ落ちるように歌う。聴く者が存在しない、無言の孤独と追憶のうちに歌い上げられる。

2. **誰かが側にいる場面**（ジョソールの暗く空虚な部屋の前）：スルマの部屋の空虚さを見せられた後、ビバの手を握り、静かに、そして意図して歌い始める。一人の残骸のようなビバに寄り添い、共に悲しみを分かち合う形で歌われる。

つまり、前者は「聴く者などいないのに独り言のように歌う」孤独な歌い方、後者は「側にいる者と結びついて歌う」共感的な歌い方であり、同じ歌が、隔絶と共有という対照的な二つの姿をとる。

answer: Rukmini failed to stop Udayaditya’s escape, but instead threw herself before King Pratapaditya and testified that the masterminds of the escape were the old king Basanta Ray, Sitaram, and the crown prince, and that Sitaram had set fire to the prison. She then personally led the soldiers, found Udayaditya in the fields, and captured him, giving the king grounds to issue the secret order to “sentence the king of Raigarh to death.” Mukhtiyar Khan went to Basanta Ray with the order in hand as he captured the crown prince, and executed him—so Rukmini’s failure to stop the escape led directly to Basanta Ray’s execution by exposing the escape and those involved, and enabling the pursuit to succeed.
answer_ja: ルクミニーはウダヤディティヤの逃亡を止められなかったが、その代わりに王プラタパディティヤの前に飛び込んで、逃亡の首謀者が老王バサンタ・ライ、シタラム、王太子の三人であることと、シタラムによる牢獄放火を証言した。さらに彼女は自ら兵を率いて野原でウダヤディティヤを発見・確保し、王に「ライガルの王に死刑を命じる」密命を下させる根拠を与えた。ムクティヤール・カーンは王太子を捕らえると同時にその命令書を携えてバサンタ・ライの元へ向かい、彼を処刑した——つまり、阻止に失敗したルクミニーが逃亡の事実と関与を暴露し追跡を成功させたことが、バサンタ・ライへの死刑執行へと直接つながった。

answer:
In Chapter 8, the welcome conveys the disparity in power naturally, without making a show of it. Pratapaditya prepares neither lights nor a nahabat; Ramchandra has only 250 attendants, and the elephants are small. During their meeting, Pratapaditya has petitions about tax revenues and reports of floods read aloud, and finally tells his son-in-law, “Come, let us go inside,” relegating him to the women’s quarters to be entertained by his wife. This is not meant as an insult; it is simply the usual business of government, and that is precisely what silently demonstrates their difference in rank. Ramchandra himself ultimately concludes that he “realized in what respects [Pratapaditya] was great.”

By contrast, in Ramchandra’s court in Chapter 19, superiority in status is performed verbally every day. They call Pratapaditya’s absent grandfather an earthworm and his son a leech; the jester and flatterers shower him with insults, and the king watches with satisfaction. In other words, the powerful have no need to show contempt, while those deemed inferior can confirm their superiority only by abusing someone who is absent. Moreover, Ramchandra cannot receive the queen at his own residence, and hides the arrangement from his courtiers. Thus, although the subordinate position assigned to him when he is told in Chapter 8 to “come inside” might seem to have been reversed in the dialogue, in reality it has only grown more entrenched. The contrast is that the fiercer the abuse, the less actual power there is.
answer_ja:
第8章での迎え方は、実力差を演じずに自然に示すものだった。プラタパディティヤは灯りもナハバットも用意せず、供も250人、象も小さく、会見中も税収の訴状や洪水の報告を読み上げ、ついには「さあ、奥へ参れ」と婿を女房のにもてなす側へ追い込む。これは侮辱の意図ではなく、あくまで通常の政務で、それこそが身分の高低を無言で証明している（ラーマチャンドラ自身も最終的に「いかなる点において偉大かを悟った」と結ぶ）。

対して第19章のラーマチャンドラの宮廷では、地位の優越が毎日、口先で演出される。不在のプラタパディティヤの祖父をミミズ、その子をヒルと罵り、道化とおべっか使いが矢を浴びせ、王はそれを見て満足する。つまり、実力のある側は侮蔑を必要とせず、格下とされた側は不在者を口汚く罵ることでしか優位を確認できない。しかもラーマチャンドラは王妃を自邸に迎えられず、その取り決めを廷臣に隠すほどで、第8章で「奥へ参れ」と席を指定された際の従属的地位は、台詞の上では逆転したはずなのに、実際にはむしろ深まっている。嘲罵の激しさと実権の不在が反比例している、という対比になっている。

answer:
Rukmini, the older widow from Raigarh who appears in Udayaditya’s past confession, later abandons Raigarh, changes her name, and hides in a corner of Jessore as the widow “Mangala.” While pretending to be an ordinary woman of no particular distinction, she patiently spends years befriending all the servants in the palace and builds a network that catches even the smallest court rumors. She continues to nurse the ambition of enthroning herself in the crown prince’s heart and ruling both his heart and the kingdom of Jessore. When word reaches the queen that she is reputed to know tantric spells and medicines, the queen sends Matangini to secretly obtain a remedy from her, hoping to win back the crown prince’s heart before driving Surma from the palace. This request brings her, long concealed, into the palace’s intrigues.

Mangala cuts roots, soaks, crushes, and mixes them, chants spells, and concocts a poison, spending five days preparing it. She also devotes much time to performing a ritual so that the crown prince will feel no pity when Surma dies. As a result, Surma drinks the poison herself and lies dying; the physician declares, “She is at her last breath,” and Udayaditya sits until dawn with Surma’s head on his lap. Her jealousy and sorcery bring about the first tragedy, taking from the crown prince the woman he loves.

Even after Surma’s death, she does not stop. She lends money at interest, manipulates people with her beauty and money, wins over the scheming half-brother Sitaram and holds secret talks with him (going so far as to say that things will not go well without Bhagavata’s help), and on a stormy night enters Udayaditya’s bedroom carrying a lamp. Finding him with a sleeping little girl in his lap, terrified by the sound of Surma’s voice, she waits for him, then tearfully tells him that he once filled her with hope and made her feel as if she were ascending to heaven, but now has left her wandering the streets like a beggar. Stabbing him with guilt, she demands, “Give me the ring on your finger,” picks up the ring he throws, and leaves. In her heart she thinks, “The enchantment of that witch has not yet been broken. After a little more time, my spells will take effect,” and waits for her next trap to work through sorcery and scheming.
answer_ja:
ウダヤディティヤの過去の告白に登場するライガルの年上未亡人ルクミニーは、以後ライガルを捨てて名を改め、未亡人「マンガラ」としてジョソールの片隅に潜む。非凡な点のないただの女を装いつつ、根気強い年ごろの努力で王宮のすべての使用人と親しくなり、宮廷の小さな噂までも摑む情報網を築いて、王太子の心に玉座を据え、彼の心とジョソール王国を同時に支配するという野望を燃やし続けていた。タントラの呪文や薬に通じているという評判が王妃の耳に入り、スルマを王宮から追放する前に王太子の心を取り戻すべく、マータンギニーを遣わして彼女から密かに薬を入手しようとした——この依頼が、久しく潜んでいた彼女を王宮の抗争に接続させる。

マンガラは木の根を切り、浸し、潰し、混ぜ、呪文を唱えて毒を調合し、五日かけて調え、さらにスルマが死ぬとき王太子の心に憐れみが生まれぬよう儀式を執り行うのに多くの時を費やした。結果としてスルマは自ら毒を飲んで死にかけ、医師に「ご臨終です」と告げられ、ウダヤディティヤは夜が明けるまでスルマの頭を膝に乗せたまま座り続けた。彼女の嫉妬と呪術が、王太子から愛する者を奪う最初の悲劇を成した。

スルマの死後も彼女は止まらない。金を貸して利子を取り、美貌と金銭で人を操い、腹違いの策略家シタラムを懐柔して密談を重ね（バーガヴァタの力を借りないとうまくいかないと語るほど）、嵐の夜にはウダヤディティヤの寝室に灯りを手に入り込む。眠る幼い女の子を膝に抱えてスルマの幻聴に怯える彼を待つと、かつて自分を希望に満たせて天に昇る気持ちにしたのに今では物乞いのように路頭に迷わせたと泣きつき、罪悪感を突き刺して「指のその指輪をくださいな」と要求し、彼の投げた指輪を拾って立ち去る。心の中では「あの魔女の呪縛はまだ解けない。もう少し時が経てば、私の呪文が効くようになるだろう」と考え、呪術と策略で次なる罠の効きを待つのである。

answer:
His initial lament was a rejection of his very birth and status: “I wish I were not the crown prince,” and “If only I were the lowliest and most insignificant of subjects.” But after enduring humiliation in the palace, his father’s searching gaze, the failure of his administration when he was no longer entrusted with governing because the people loved him, and the freedom and warmth he found with his great-uncle in Raigarh (compounded by his downfall after meeting Rukmini), his lament over his status changed into self-reproach: “I am weak, and my weakness brought about this ruin.”

In Chapter 34, on the journey home after losing his great-uncle, he goes three days without eating, sleeping, or even blinking, thinking all the while. At last he cries, “What ruin has occurred because of me?” and “The weak are of no use to the world,” and declares that he will leave the world. Brought before his father as a captive, he can no longer even look at him, and admits, “I am not fit for this kingdom.” His father, too, wants him deposed, and with both of them in agreement, Udayaditya touches the feet of the goddess Kali and swears an oath before her, declaring, “I will accept not so much as a clod of earth from the kingdom, nor touch the throne or the scepter.” In return, he asks not to be confined in prison, to be allowed to wander to Kashi, and for funds to build a pilgrims’ rest house and temple bearing his great-uncle’s name.

Thus, his initial wish that he had never been born is ultimately fulfilled in reality as a formal vow of renunciation: after taking sole responsibility for the ruin and becoming convinced that it is impossible for a weak man to sit on the throne, he renounces his right of succession and royal authority in full before the gods, and changes his status from a man of the world to a pilgrim. The decisive difference is that his lament remained an expression of emotion, whereas his final renunciation takes the institutional and religious form of an agreement with his father and an oath before the gods.
answer_ja:
初期の嘆きは「王太子でなければよかった」「最も小さく取るに足らない民であったなら」という、生まれ持った身分そのものへの拒絶だった。しかし王宮での屈辱、父上の試す眼差し、民に慕われたために統治を任されなくなった政務の失敗、そしてライガルの大おじ様のもとでの自由と温もり（そこにルクミニーとの出会いによる転落も重なる）を経て、身分への嘆きは「自分が弱者であり、その弱さゆえに破滅を招いた」という自責の感情へと変質する。

第34章では、大おじ様を失った後の帰途、三日間食事をせず、眠りも瞬きもせずただ考え続けた末に「私のせいで、何という破滅が起きたのか」「弱者は世に益がない」と叫び、世を去ると宣言する。捕虜として父の前に出された彼は、もはや父の顔を見ることもできず、「私はこの王国にふさわしくない」と自ら不適合を認める。父もまた彼の廃位を望んでおり、その合意の上でウダヤディティヤはカーリー女神の御御足に触れて神前に誓いを立て、「王国の土一かけらたりとも受け取らず、玉座にも王笏にも触れない」と明言する。代償として要求したのは、牢に閉じ込められることの拒否と、カーシーへの放浪と、大おじ様の名を冠した巡礼者宿と寺の建立資金である。

つまり初期の「生まれなければよかった」という願いは、破滅の責任を一身に負う自責と、「弱者が王座に立つことの不可能」の確信を経て、正式な放棄誓言——神前での相続権・王権の全面放棄と、世俗から巡礼者への身分転換——として現実に成就する。嘆きが感情の言葉にとどまっていたのに対し、最終的な放棄は父との合意と神誓という制度的・宗教的形式をとる点に決定的な違いがある。

answer: Although Nayan Chand carried the letter to Jessore, he was afraid and gave it to the queen rather than to Pratapaditya. The queen could not tell either Vibha or the Maharaja, so she consulted Basanta Ray. Basanta Ray said, “Honor is no concern; send her to her husband’s home at once,” and advised the queen to spread a rumor throughout the household that “Ramchandra has sent a letter asking that Vibha be sent to Chandradwip.” The queen told Vibha and the household this, concealing the actual letter—the threat of divorce. Vibha was delighted, mistakenly believing that her husband had forgiven her and was coming to fetch her. Later, she began pleading with her mother, “When will you send me?”
answer_ja: ナヤンチャンドがジョソールへ手紙を携えたものの恐れて、プラタパディティヤの手ではなく王妃の手にそれを渡した。王妃はビバにもマハラジャにも言えず、バサンタ・ライに相談した。バサンタ・ライは「名誉など問題ではない、すぐ嫁ぎ先へ送れ」と言い、屋敷中に「ラーマチャンドラがビバをチャンドラドウィープへ送ってほしいと手紙を寄越した」という噂を流すよう王妃に勧めた。王妃はそれをビバと屋敷中に告げ、事実の（離縁脅迫の）手紙は伏せた。ビバは夫が自分を許し、迎えに来てくれたのだと誤解して喜び、後に母のもとへ「いつ送ってくださるの」と願うようになった。

answer: Pratapaditya set a trap by blocking the canal beside the palace—the mooring place for Ramchandra’s boat—with a large sal tree log, and shutting the doors so that no one could leave the inner palace. But Udayaditya escaped by leaping over the palace wall, then lowered Ramchandra from the rooftop to the boat using a rope made of cloth. The boat was unable to move through the waterway blocked by the log, but the guards’ stones could not reach it, and they were confused and distracted when they could not find the gun’s priming powder. Taking advantage of this, the party dragged the boat over the log. The pursuit boats were also delayed because the man sent to fetch them stopped to smoke at Harimudi’s shop and wake Ramshankar to collect a debt. As a result, Ramchandra’s boat reached the Bhairava River before dawn and made its escape.
answer_ja: プラタパディティヤは、王宮に隣接する運河（ラーマチャンドラの船の停泊地）を大きなサールの木の丸太で塞ぎ、奥御殿からも誰も出られないよう扉を閉ざして罠を仕掛けた。しかしウダヤディティヤが城壁を飛び越えて脱出し、屋上から布で作った綱を垂らしてラーマチャンドラを舟へ降ろした。舟は丸太で塞がれた水路で動けなくなるが、見張りは石を投げても届かず、鉄砲の火口が見つからず取り合わずに混乱している隙に、一行は丸太の上を舟を引きずって越えていった。追跡用の舟も、呼びに往った者がハリムディーの店でタバコを吸い、ラムシャンカルを起こして借金の取り立てをするなど足止めされたため遅れ、ラーマチャンドラの船は夜明け前にバイラヴァ川へ達して脱出に成功した。

answer:
Basanta Ray’s relationship with his sitar reflects his despair in stages.

First, in the farewell scene in Chapter 13, the sitar is the very embodiment of the most delicate part of his heart. When he has to part from Udayaditya, he strums the sitar furiously, but at the sight of Biba and Surma in tears, the sound catches in his throat, and he is finally forced to stop playing. This moment, when his emotions are so overwhelming that even music becomes impossible, shows that the pain of losing those he loves has begun to break him from within. Then he leaves the sitar behind. His words, “I shall play the sitar no more,” amount to a declaration that, along with his sorrow, he has also let go of joy—in effect, renouncing the will to live.

In Chapter 27, this meaning deepens further. After learning of Udayaditya’s imprisonment, Basanta Ray says that the sitar is “there, but its strings are broken, and it cannot be tuned.” Here, the broken strings directly symbolize the severing of his bonds with Udayaditya, Biba, and the others he loves. The sitar, with its broken strings, can no longer be tuned, reflecting a state in which his heart, too, can no longer be set right.

Furthermore, in the scene where he, who once sang joyfully, murmurs alone toward the setting sun, “I alone, the only one, have been left behind,” singing itself has become empty. Songs well up, but there is no one to hear them; music remains, but joy is gone—this state shows that his despair has advanced beyond mere grief into a void in which his connection to the meaning of the world has been severed. In other words, the sitar is the clearest mirror of how Udayaditya’s absence has turned his heart into “strings that can no longer be tuned.”
answer_ja:
バサンタ・ライのシタールとの関係は、彼の絶望を段階的に映し出している。

まず第13章での別れの場面では、シタールは彼の心の最も繊細な部分そのものだった。ウダヤディティヤと離れなければならない時、彼はシタールを激しく掻き鳴らすが、ビバとスルマの涙を見て音が詰まり、ついに演奏をやめざるを得なくなる。感情が余りすぎて音楽すら成立しなくなったこの瞬間は、愛する者を失う痛みが彼の内側を壊し始めていることを示している。そして彼はシタールを置いて行く。「もうシタールは弾かん」という言葉は、悲しみと共に喜びもまた手放した、いわば生への意欲の放棄宣告である。

第27章では、その意味がさらに深まる。ウダヤディティヤの投獄を知った後のバサンタ・ライは、シタールを「あるが、弦が切れて音を合わせられない」と語る。ここでは弦の断絶が、そのまま彼とウダヤディティヤ・ビバら愛する者たちとの絆の断絶を象徴している。弦が切れたシタールは、もはや調律できず、彼の心ももう整えられないという状態を映す。

さらに、かつては喜びの中で歌っていた彼が、「私だけが、ただ一人残された」と夕日に向かって独り口ずさむ場面では、歌うこと自体が空虚化している。歌は湧いてくるが聞く者がいない、音楽は残っても喜びがない——というこの状態は、彼の絶望が単なる悲嘆ではなく、世界との意味の連絡が断たれた虚無へと進んだことを示す。すなわちシタールは、ウダヤディティヤの不在によって、彼の心が「調律不能な弦」へと変わったことの最も明確な鏡なのである。

answer:
Udayaditya was once known for fearlessly confronting oppression at the risk of his life and trying to save the people by restraining officials without regard for the consequences. But after Surma’s death, his attitude changed dramatically.

- **Avoiding intervention**: When he hears the order to raid, loot, and set fire to the Chapra landlord’s office at night, he has his horse prepared and heads for the inner palace, but after agonizing over it, he says, “I’m not going anywhere,” and abandons his departure.
- **Indifference to the people’s cries**: Even when he sees people tied to trees and beaten by officials, crying, “Your Highness, please save us!”, he can only flee inside the building, unable to bear their suffering; he no longer tries to rescue them as he once did.
- **Withholding financial support**: Even when Bhagavata and Sitaram’s salaries are stopped, he lacks the courage to send them money secretly. Though he thinks, “I’ll send it to him today,” in the end he does not.

The reason behind this is not a growing attachment to life, but a blind fear of Pratapaditya. He feels as though the king holds his entire fate in his hands, and has become hesitant and suspicious about everything. He has lost his ability to act on his own, as though even when standing at death’s door, a frown from the king could bring him back to life.
answer_ja:
かつてのウダヤディティヤは、危険をものともせず圧政に対して命がけで立ち向かい、結果を顧みずに役人を制止して民を救おうとする評判の存在だった。だがスルマの死後（のこの頃）、その姿勢は大きく豹変した。

- **介入の回避**: チャプラの地主の役場への夜襲・略奪・放火の命令を聞くと、馬を準備して奥御殿へ向かうが、思い悩った末に「どこへも行かぬ」と言って出発をやめる。
- **民の悲鳴への無関心**: 役人に木に縛り殴られ「王太子様、お助けを！」と叫ぶ民を見ても、苦痛に耐えきれず建物の中に逃げ込むだけで、以前のように救おうとはしない。
- **金銭的支援の停止**: バーガヴァタとシタラムの俸給が止められても、密かに金を送る勇気が持てず、「今日にでも送ってやろう」と思っても結局送らない。

その背景にあるのは、命への執着の増大ではなく、プラタパディティヤへの盲目的な恐怖である。王の掌中に自分の運命のすべてが握られているかのように感じ、何事にも躊躇し、疑念を抱くようになり、たとえ死の淵にあっても眉をひそめられれば生き返らされるかの如く、自発的な行動力を失っていた。

answer: He fabricated (or took advantage of) a fire, setting the guardhouse near the prison ablaze. While all the guards rushed to put it out, he went alone to the prison, carried Udayaditya out, and helped him escape into the fields.
answer_ja: 火事をでっち上げ（または利用）して牢獄に近い衛兵小屋に燃え上がらせ、見張りの衛兵が皆消火に殺到したすきに単身牢を訪れ、ウダヤディティヤを抱えるようにして外へ連れ出し、野原へと脱出させた。

answer:
**Act 1 (Escape from the rooftop):** Rammohan twisted and tied together the thick cloth from the inner palace to make one enormous rope, then fastened it to a pillar on the rooftop. He tied Ramachandra Rai to his back, climbed down the rope, and, at the end of it, clenched it between his teeth as he lowered the king from his back, then lowered him into the boat with both hands. He then jumped down himself.

**Act 2 (Departure from the palace):** As they came to receive Bibha, the jester Ramai Bhand insulted the queen, so Rammohan grabbed him by the scruff of the neck and forcibly threw him out of the room, then told the king he was resigning from his service. He lifted the limp, unconscious Bibha into the palanquin waiting at the doorway and carried her off to the boat.
answer_ja:
第1幕（屋上からの脱出）：ラムモハンは奥御殿の厚布をねじり結んで一本の巨大な綱を作り、屋上の柱に結びつけた。ラーマチャンドラ・ライを背中に縛りつけ、綱を伝って降り、綱端で歯で食いしばって王を背中から下ろし、両手で舟へ下ろした後、自らも飛び降りた。

第2幕（王宮からの退去）：ビバを迎える場面で、道化のラマイ・バンドが王妃を侮辱したため、ラムモハンは彼の首根っこを掴んで力づくで部屋から放り出し、王に奉公を辞すると告げた。ぐったりと気を失ったビバを抱き起こし、戸口の駕籠の一気に乗せて船へと運び出した。

answer:
In Chapter 8, Vibha is forced by the queen to dress in extravagant formal attire. She wears eight thick gold bangles and a huge diamond bracelet, an oversized nose ornament that does not suit her, and a hairstyle the queen has redone against her wishes. To Vibha, the outfit feels like a burden, mingling joy with bewilderment. Her own tastes—such as pale turquoise bangles that set off her youthful white arms, and a nose ornament suited to her small face—are entirely overridden; the attire is the queen’s will imposed upon her. Even so, her joy shines through in her face and mouth, so plainly that even the Crown Prince can see it.

By contrast, when she goes to Ramchandra in Chandradwip in Chapters 36–37, she no longer wants anything resembling a queen’s attire. She even refuses a palanquin and leaves the boat dressed like a humble woman, “like one of the common people, like a beggar woman.” Her veil is disheveled, and she walks through the crowd looking almost barefoot. No one welcomes her with respect; guards seize her, and she is brought into the palace like a servant.

In short, her attire changes dramatically from “splendid yet awkward formal dress, bearing the royal grandeur and her mother-in-law’s will” to “the miserable, beggar-like appearance of someone who has cast aside her rank and finery and exposed her identity.” At the same time, her inner state shifts from a face filled with irrepressible, radiant joy to one of despair and listlessness, feeling that everything she sees is false as she is consumed by shame. The loss of her finery embodies how she has lost, like a mirage, her hopes for happiness in the palace.
answer_ja:
第8章では、ビバは王妃に无理やり派手な正装をさせられていた。太い金の腕輪を八本と巨大なダイヤモンドの腕飾り、似合わない大きな鼻飾り、そして王妃に結び直された気に入らない髪型で、本人は喜びと困惑を交えた重荷のような装いだった。若々しい白い腕に映える薄いトルコ石色の腕輪や、自分の小さな顔に合わない鼻飾りといった本人の趣味は完全に押し流され、装いは王妃の意図の押しつけ物だった。それでも彼女の喜びは顔や口元からにじみ出て、王太子にも見透かされるほどの晴れやかさがあった。

一方、第36〜37章でチャンドラドウィープのラーマチャンドラのもとへ行く時、彼女はもはや王妃らしい装いを一切望まなかった。輿すら拒み、「一介の民のように、物乞いの女のように」と、質素な女の身なりで船から出て、ヴェールも乱れて素足のような姿で人混みの中を歩いていく。誰も丁重に迎えず、衛兵に掴まれ、召使同然に宮殿に入った。

つまり、装いは「王家の威光と姑の意志を一身にまとった、輝かしいがぎこちない正装」から、「地位も装飾もかなぐり捨てた、乞食のような惨めで身元さらけ出す身なり」へと劇的に変化している。同時に内面も、抑えきれない晴れやかな喜びに満ちた顔から、恥ずかしさで死ぬ思いで目に入るものすべてが偽りに感じられる、絶望と無気力な姿へと反転している。装いの剥落は、彼女が王宮の幸福への望みを蜃気楼のように失ったことを体現している。

answer:
In the bedchamber, the window was a window of “absence.” The memory of Surma sitting there was etched into it, and he looked toward that vacant place with the illusion and expectation that the dead might appear at any moment. In other words, it symbolized the sorrow of waiting forever for the dead to return, knowing they would never come. He sat by the window and tried to confirm his connection to the departed through the moonlight, the garden, and the unchanging wind, but the only thing the window returned was the fact that “she will not come.”

In prison, by contrast, the window became a window of “liberation” and “innate freedom.” A tiny opening offering a bamboo grove, a Shiva temple, and a fragment of sky connected him to the infinite sky where birds flew; simply looking at the window became proof that he was free by nature. That is why he avoided the bed and sat on the floor, clinging to the window. The soft bedding itself was the real prison, while only the sky beyond the window promised a future in which his shackles would break.

Thus, the window changes from **“a boundary of memory and despair,” where he waits endlessly for a lost other,** into **“proof of his own freedom,” bringing hope independently of others.** In addition, whereas the bedchamber window was a passive place that fostered the illusion that “Surma might be there if he opened it,” the prison window was the only source of light in the dark room that he could deliberately choose to look at. It also came to overlap with the symbol of “all the doors of the prison” opening with Biva’s arrival.
answer_ja:
寝室期の窓は「不在」の窓だった。そこにスルマが座っていた記憶が刻まれ、空けたままのその場所へ向けて、今にも亡き人が現れる幻と期待を抱く場所――つまり、死者の再来を待ち続けながら、いつまでも来ないという悲哀の象徴である。彼は窓辺に腰を下ろし、月明かりや庭園、変わらぬ風の中に、去った者とのつながりを確かめようとするが、窓が返すのは「来ない」という事実だけだった。

牢獄期の窓は逆に、「解放」と「本来の自由」の窓に変わる。竹藪とシヴァ寺院と一片の空というごく小さな開口部が、鳥の飛ぶ無限の空と結びつき、窓を見ていること自体が、自分がもともと自由であるという確証になる。ゆえに彼は寝台を避け、床に座って窓にしがみつく。柔らかい寝具こそが本当の牢獄であり、窓の向こうの空だけが、足枷が壊れる未来を保証する。

つまり窓は、**失われた他者を待ち続ける「記憶と絶望の境界」**から、**他者に依存せず自立的に希望をもたらす「自己の自由の証」**へと変質している。加えて、寝室期の窓は「開けばスルマがいるかもしれない」という幻を抱かせる消極的な場所だったのに対し、牢獄期の窓は、暗闇の部屋の中で唯一、彼が自ら意図的に見ることを選べる光源であり、ビバの訪れとともに開かれる「牢のすべての扉」の象徴とも重なる。

answer:
In Chapter 21, Sitaram comes to see Rukmini, who is manipulated by her beauty and money, and, while borrowing money, keeps making excuses, saying, “I’ll definitely pay you back tomorrow.” Rukmini is both a business partner who lends money at interest and a woman obsessed with Udayaditya, while Sitaram tries to win her over with jokes and wit. Here, money is a tool of negotiation, and their relationship is still at the stage of playful flirtation.

Before long, their relationship turns into a joint conspiracy. Sitaram confers secretly with Rukmini to devise a scheme and, with her help, becomes involved in the crown prince’s imprisonment and escape. In Chapter 31, Sitaram uses a fire to burn down the prison, fakes the crown prince’s death, and plots his escape. He also visits the hut to try to make off with Rukmini’s money, and discovers that the person there is Mangala herself. Rukmini erupts in anger, saying she has “returned from Yama’s gates,” and accuses Sitaram of conspiring with the crown prince and ruining her hopes. As she chases him, demanding a butcher’s cleaver, Sitaram realizes that figurative jokes will not work and runs off, afraid she will cut off his head.

In short, the outward financial arrangement of lending and borrowing becomes a conspiracy in which their interests align over the crown prince; then betrayal arises within the conspiracy when Sitaram’s arson and escape come to light. Rukmini cannot recover the position and future she has lost, while Sitaram realizes that unless he silences this witness, he will destroy himself. Their resentment and fear converge, and their relationship deteriorates into one in which each seeks the other’s life.
answer_ja:
第21章では、シタラムは美貌と金銭で操られるルクミニーに会いに来ており、金を借りながら「明日には必ず返す」と言い訳を重ねる。ルクミニーは利息を取る商売の相手であると同時に、ウダヤディティヤへの執着を抱く女であり、シタラムは冗談と機知で彼女の心を掴もうとする。ここで金銭は駆け引きの道具であり、関係は戯れと色気の段階にある。

やがて関係は共同謀略へ変わる。シタラムは策略を立てるためにルクミニーと密談し、彼女の助けを借りて王太子の投獄や脱走に関与する。第31章では、シタラムは火事を利用して牢を燃やし、王太子の死をでっち上げて逃亡を企てる。彼はついでにルクミニーの金も掠めようと小屋を訪れ、そこにいるのがマンガラ本人だと知る。ルクミニーは「ヤマの門から戻ってきた」と怒りを爆発させ、シタラムが王太子と結託して自分の望みを台無しにしたと責める。肉切り包丁を求めて追う彼女に対し、シタラムは比喩的な冗談が通用しないと悟り、首をはねられることを恐れて逃げ出す。

つまり、貸し借りという表向きの金銭関係は、王太子を巡る利害が一致した共謀に変わり、やがて共謀の内部で裏切り（シタラムの放火と逃亡の露見）が生じる。ルクミニーは捨てられた地位と未来を挽回できず、シタラムはその証人を消さなければ自滅すると悟る。仇恨と恐怖が噛み合い、互いが命を狙う関係へと落ちていく。

answer:
After luring Basanta Ray outside the mansion in the middle of the night, Sitaram used the fire as “the opening move in the escape.” The guards rushed first to the guardhouse, where their bedding and belongings were kept, and while the watch on the prince’s room was reduced to a mere formality, Sitaram himself entered the prison, claimed that “the prison is on fire,” and led the prince out as if carrying him.

From there, the scheme expanded in three stages. First, obstructing the firefighting. Sitaram’s accomplices blended in with the firefighting party, poured water where there was no fire, went to fetch water and did not return, smashed water jars, raised a commotion, and threw themselves against people, spreading the fire and sustaining the confusion. Second, fabricating evidence. They set fire one after another to the windows, doors, beams, rafters, gateposts, and wooden fencing of the now-empty prison cell itself, while Sitaram threw bones and a skull, as well as the sword he had received from the prince, into the room. Third, staging eyewitness accounts. Getting there first, he shouted that “the prince’s cries can be heard from inside the prison” and that “the roof has collapsed and the cries have stopped,” prompting the guards themselves to give eyewitness accounts of “the prince in the flames,” “the cries,” and “the charred remains of a sword.”

Sitaram also spread rumors to establish the belief that “the prince died in the fire,” and destroyed the letters to the prince that could be discarded among the three, erasing traces. The fact that a woman who tried to tell the truth was beaten and thrown aside by the crowd, and no one listened to her, also helped the cover-up. Thus the diversion was completed as an official “confirmation of death,” with all four elements in place—flames, a corpse, testimony, and letters—and the king, too, believed the prince was dead and ordered a pursuit to Raigarh.
answer_ja:
バサンタ・ライを夜中に屋敷の外へおびき出した後、シタラムは火事を「脱獄の幕開け」として用いた。衛兵たちは自身の寝具・家財が置かれた衛兵詰所の火に真っ先に駆けつけ、王太子の部屋の見張りが名ばかりになった隙に、シタラム自ら牢へ入って「牢獄に火がつく」と称し、王子を抱えるようにして外へ連れ出した。

そこから工作は三段階で拡大した。第一に、消火の妨害。シタラムの仲間が消火隊にまぎれ込み、水のない場所へ水をかけ、水を取りに行って戻らず、水瓶を割り、騒ぎ立てて人に倒れかかって火を拡大させ、混乱を持続させた。第二に、証拠の捏造。空になった王子の牢そのものに窓・扉・梁・垂木・門柱・木柵へ次々と火を付け、シタラムが骨や頭蓋骨、そして王子から受け取った剣を部屋の中に投げ込んだ。第三に、目撃の演出。先回りして「牢の中から王子の叫び声が聞こえる」「屋根が崩れ落ちて声が止まった」と叫び、衛兵たち自身に「炎の中の王子」「叫び声」「焼けただれた剣の残骸」という目撃証言を引き出させた。

さらにシタラムは噂を流して「火事で王子は死んだ」という見方を定着させ、王子宛の三通の手紙のうち破棄できるものを処分して痕跡を消した。真相を話そうとした女が民衆に殴り捨てられ誰にも聞かれなかったことも、この隠蔽を助けた。こうして目くらましは、炎・死体・証言・手紙の四つを揃えた公式な「死亡確認」へと完成し、王も王子の死を信じてライガルへの追討を命じる結果になった。

answer: He interpreted Udayaditya’s actions as having been done to help his own sister (Biba), not to save Ramchandra Ray’s life. So he felt no gratitude; he thought, “That was only natural. It would have been strange if it had turned out otherwise,” and ignored Udayaditya’s merit, making him the butt of jokes at court.
answer_ja: ウダヤディティヤは自分の妹（ビバ）のために自分を助けたのであって、自分の命を救うことがウダヤディティヤの目的ではなかった、と解釈した。したがって感謝はせず、「それは当然のことだ。そうならない方がおかしい」と考え、彼の功績を無視して宮廷で冗談の種にした。

answer:
Initially dismissed as “not a threat,” the authority of the Emperor of Delhi ultimately became the instrument used to corner the prince.

In Chapter 22, Bhagavata and Sitaram fabricate a false petition that makes it seem as though Crown Prince Udayaditya is accusing his father, Pratapaditya, of treason against the Emperor and pleading to obtain the kingdom for himself. They stamp it with the Crown Prince’s seal from the ring Rukmini brought, and Bhagavata gives it not to Delhi but to Pratapaditya himself, falsely claiming that he had seized it when one of Udayaditya’s servants tried to flee with the petition to Delhi.

In other words, they turn the political threat of an appeal to the Emperor against the prince: by making the king believe that the Crown Prince is appealing to the Emperor in an attempt to remove his father, they use the Emperor’s authority as a pretext to purge and imprison the son. The threat the minister warned of in Chapter 2—“the Emperor of Delhi’s wrath means fifty thousand troops”—instead becomes fuel for the king’s fear, fanning the flames of suspicion toward his son.
answer_ja:
当初「脅威ではない」と一蹴されたディリーシュワル（デリー皇帝）は、その裁き権限こそが最後には王子を追い込む装置として機能した。

第22章でバーガヴァタとシタラムは、王太子ウダヤディティヤが父プラタパディティヤを皇帝への反逆罪で告発し、自ら王国を得ようと嘆願しているかのような偽の嘆願書を作成する。ルクミニーが持ち込んだ指輪の王太子の印章を押印し、それをバーガヴァタはデリーへは向かわずにプラタパディティヤ本人に渡し、「ウダヤディティヤの家来が嘆願書をデリーへ持ち逃げしようとしたところ奪い取った」と偽って提出した。

つまり、皇帝のもとへ訴えられるという政治的脅威そのものを逆手に取り、王太子が皇帝にすがって父を排除しようとしていると王に信じ込ませることで、皇帝の権威を口実に息子を粛清・投獄させる手段へと転用したのである。第2章で大臣が警告した「ディリーシュワルの怒り＝五万の兵」という脅威は、王の恐怖心を刺激する材料として、かえって息子への疑心を燃やす火種になった。

answer: The way Vibha’s hair is dressed serves as a visible marker of Surma’s presence and absence. While Surma is by her side, Vibha’s hair is tied as she herself likes. It is her sole voluntary resistance to the Queen’s forceful adornment—the thick gold bangles, the large nose ornament, and the imposed hairstyle—and a sign of Surma’s affection and their closeness. Unable to endure the hairstyle the Queen had arranged, Vibha secretly went back to Surma to have it redone; her hair thus became a symbol of her trust in Surma and of tastes and independence distinct from the Queen’s. After Surma’s death, this daily ritual becomes proof of her absence. When it is time to dress her hair, Vibha sits silently, motionless, as if waiting for Surma to come and do it. Surma, who once embraced her around the neck and comforted her as soon as Vibha’s face clouded even slightly, no longer comes to dress her hair, and evening and night fall. The repeated absence of someone to dress her hair makes the reality of Surma’s death and the collapse of Vibha’s heart visible each day. Thus, her hair bears the imprint of Surma’s presence in life; after her death, the ritual’s cessation—the fact that there is no one to dress it—becomes a marker that renews the tragedy of her absence every day.
answer_ja: ビバの髪の結い方は、スルマの存在と不在を目視できる印として機能している。スルマがそばにいる間、髪はビバ自身の好きなように結ばれ、王妃の強い装い（太い金の腕輪、大きな鼻飾り、強制された髪型）に対する唯一の自主的な抵抗であり、スルマの愛情と二人の親密さを示すものだった。王妃が結んだ髪型をビバが耐えられず、こっそりスルマのところへ行き直したことで、髪はスルマへの信頼と、王妃とは異なる趣味・自立の象徴となった。スルマの死後、この日課は不在の証明に変わる。結う時間になってもビバは黙って座り、今にもスルマが来て結んでくれるのを待つかのように動かない。かつてはビバの顔が少しでも曇れば、すぐに首に抱きついて慰めてくれたスルマが、髪を結ってくれないまま夕暮れと夜が来る――髪を結ってもらえないという反復される欠如が、スルマの死の実感と、ビバの心の崩壊を日々可視化している。したがって髪は、スルマの生前の存在を刻み、その死後は「結ってくれる者がいない」という行為の停止を通して、悲劇的な不在を毎日新たにする目印なのである。
